item.description:
Discover what makes Métis beadwork unique and create your own work of art! In this workshop, participants will learn about the history of Métis beadwork and the symbolism behind each bead used. Attendees will discover how historical beadwork patterns led to a new form of pointillism, where every dot of paint represents a bead. Participants will explore this contemporary art form by creating their own bead art painting to take home. No experience needed. item.title: A Concert in the Ruins of St. Anne’s Church: Wavelength w/ Völur / Charles Spearin & the Local Singers with Fleshtone Aura / A Horse Named Friday / BODY////GRAVE — Thu Aug 27, 8:00 PM — Ruins of St. Anne's Church
item.description:
Presented with Sonic Boom
Völur
(Toronto // ambient drone-folk)
Charles Spearin & the Local Singers with Fleshtone Aura
(Toronto // experimental sound surprises from Broken Social Scene/Do Make Say Think co-founder and friends)
A Horse Named Friday
(Kitchener // chamber folk)
+ BODY////GRAVE (Toronto // DJ project debut by Justin Small of Do Make Say Think)
In association with the art exhibition “Where Walls Meet Sky”
In June 2024 St. Anne’s Anglican Church was destroyed by a tragic fire. A unique and beautiful space, the church held meaning to the generations of families in Toronto’s Little Portugal Neighbourhood, and the fire was a devastating loss for the community.
Located amidst the reconstruction, A Concert in the Ruins of St. Anne’s Church is a one-night-only collaboration between Wavelength Music and “gallery without walls” Art Spin. This will be a contemplative experience under the stars as we think about renewal and collective remembrance.

item.title: Toronto Country Fest: Propter Hawk — Thu Aug 27, 8:30 PM — Trinity Stage
item.description:
Fronted by vocal powerhouse Malorie Jo Blake, Propter Hawk is a five-piece Toronto rock group whose cinematic, road-worn music is as fitting for packed dance floors as it is for the closing moments of a long night. The band is built from a formidable lineup of veteran musicians drawn from northern mining towns and big city boroughs, grounding their sound in life experience, grit and groove. Now back in their rehearsal studio—known affectionately as the “Loveshack”—Propter Hawk are heading into their next chapter. With new material on the horizon and a growing reputation, the band stands poised for a future that honours rock and roll’s past while pushing it boldly forward.
Source: Distillery District

item.description:

A regular presence in Toronto’s music scene, the band plays rooms including the Cameron House, Dakota Tavern, and Horseshoe Tavern. On July 17, they released their self-titled debut album, showcasing a blend of alt-country, folk, and red-dirt roots rock. item.title: Distillery Country Music Series: Lucas Mason — Mon Aug 31, 1:00 PM — Trinity Stage
item.description:
Lucas Mason is a 19-year-old singer-songwriter from Ontario and one of Canada’s promising new voices in country and folk. He gained international attention in 2024 after joining Zach Bryan on stage in a viral moment captured by millions of views. Since then, Lucas has performed at major festivals, including Big Valley Jamboree, Misty City Music Festival, North of Nowhere and Sauble Beach Party, as well as the Hamilton Tiger-Cats Halftime Show and The Horseshoe Tavern. Inspired by Zach Bryan, Tyler Childers and Bob Dylan, Lucas brings raw honesty to his songwriting. His debut album arrives in November 2026, with four singles already earning playlist cover features across Apple Music, Amazon Music and Spotify.

Her Sophomore release Cutting Through The Noise – is a bold, bright reimagining of North American roots music as diverse and defiant as the songwriter who made it. Rich with ethereal soundscapes and earthy, organic arrangements-it’s a gorgeous blend of Celtic, folk, traditional country, Appalachian bluegrass, and atmospheric Americana, all tied together by a woman whose voice has earned comparisons to Dolly Parton and Alison Krauss.

item.title: Creative Writing For Newcomers — Mon Sep 14, 1:00 PM — Toronto Reference Library
item.description:
This program provides a supportive, low-pressure environment where newcomers can build confidence in their English writing, communication, and presentation skills. Together, we will: 1. Have a short, collective discussion period. 2. Begin writing based on a prompt from the instructor (Example: This year, I learned... Last week, I did... Something funny happened when…) 3. Present what we wrote to the group. Please note: This is a group meeting. We do not offer individual lessons. We will not be spell-checking, looking at punctuation, grammar, ect. We will be focusing on basic sentence structure and presentation.
Source: Toronto Public Library — Young Adults
